To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified new actinomycetal diversity from marine sediment samples collected off the California coast and that Salinispora spp., previously reported from more tropical marine environments, were found in sediments from deep-sea sites.
we have identified eight new actinomycetal OTUs from marine sediments and have found Salinispora spp., previously thought to be tropical in origin, in deep-sea marine samples.

(1) the Streptomyces genus is more diverse and widespread in marine sediment than previously thought, (2) Salinispora sequences were detected in marine sediments >1100 m and (3) Salinispora spp., which are known to be potent producers of bioactive natural products, were not successfully isolated from deep-sea marine sediment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new actinomycetota from marine environments and the development of methods to culture these organisms.
the identification and characterization of new marine actinomycin producers and their potential to produce bioactive compounds.
the isolation and characterization of novel marine-derived actinomycetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Salinispora are present in marine sediments at all latitudes and at all depths.
actinomycetal diversity in marine sediments is much greater than currently recognized and that Salinispora spp., in particular, are more widely distributed than previously thought.
actinomycetous bacteria are widely distributed in the marine environment, but the majority remain uncultured.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that there is a high diversity of actinomycetic bacteria in the marine environment, that this diversity is not well represented in the current culture collections, and that the distribution of Salinispora is broader than previously thought.
the diversity of marine actinomysetes is not limited to tropical environments and that the diversity in marine sediments may be greater than currently appreciated.

the actinomycetal diversity within marine sediments is greater than previously appreciated and that the distribution of some of the more interesting actinomycetous genera is broader than currently recognized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
targeted searches for actinomcyetes using 16S rRNA gene sequencing are effective for identifying novel actinomycetal diversity.
targeted searches for marine actinomyscetes can yield new diversity and that Salinispora spp., in particular, may be more widely distributed than previously thought.
culture-based approaches are likely to miss a significant portion of the actinomycetemicrobiota in the environment.
